newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil companies weigh new crisis measures.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil companies weigh new crisis measures.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company and U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp are considering new emergency measures after a new wave of attacks on a main oil pipeline, company officials said Monday.

The 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity pipeline which runs from the Cano Limon field in northeast Colombia to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas was dynamited by leftist rebels twice over the weekend and was broken at another point by a landslide, an Ecopetrol spokesman said.

Pumping along the pipeline, the second largest in Colombia, has been suspended since Wednesday after an attack last week. Occidental has limited on-site storage capacity at the Cano Limon field and could be forced to shut-in production later Monday, a company official said.
He said the company was also considering declaring force majeure in the field -- a decision was due early Monday afternoon.
A spokesman for Ecopetrol, which is an associate partner with Occidental in the Cano Limon field, said production had been reduced over the weekend but was unable to say to what level.

The pipeline bombings, carried out by suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels took place 41 miles (67 km) and 218 miles (350 km) west of the Cano Limon field. The landslide occured 79 miles (127 km) west of the field.
